defects.summary: `_unquote` strips quotes from glob metacharacters, so a QUOTED catch-all `"*")` — which bash treats as a literal asterisk, not a catch-all — satisfies `assert "*" in literals`. The suite goes green on a workflow whose unknown-verdict annotation is dead. The pre-change scanner caught this; this commit removes that coverage.
defects.evidence: bash: `case wat in "*") echo hit;; esac` prints nothing, exit 0 — a quoted star matches only a literal `*`. Splicing `_arm('  *)', '  "*)"')` (and the `'*'` form) into the real body: `bash -n` rc=0, and `test_the_case_block_names_every_status_the_module_knows()` PASSES GREEN on both. Running the same two fixtures through the base-commit scanner (b81f6f1, reimplemented verbatim) gives `AssertionError: no catch-all` on both — so this is a regression, not a pre-existing gap. Runtime proof of the harm: `verdict="brand-new-status"` against the quoted catch-all produced stdout='' and rc=0 — no `::warning::`, run green, exactly the failure `assert "*" in literals` exists to prevent. Aggravating: the commit's own new `quoted-literals` fixture (line 419, `"fresh"|'unavailable'|"$drift")`) actively teaches that quoting a case pattern is "a reformat bash cannot see" — true for `fresh`, false for `*`, so the fixture set invites the exact edit that trips this.

defects.summary: `_splice` re-imposes the exact line-shape anchor the commit removed from the scanner. Apply the `opener-shares-its-line` reformat — the one fixture #3 declares must not red — to the real workflow and 28 tests error with an inscrutable `ValueError`, a worse message than the assertion it replaced.
defects.evidence: Lines 361-362: `start = lines.index('case "$verdict" in')` / `end = lines.index("esac", start)` require the shipped file's opener and closer to be lines reading exactly that text. I applied the blessed reformat to `.github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml` (`case "$verdict" in stale|missing|unreadable)` on one line) and ran the file: `28 failed, 137 passed`, every one `E ValueError: 'case "$verdict" in' is not in list` raised inside `_splice`. The old anchor at least said "the audit step's `case` opener is no longer a line of its own"; this says nothing about the workflow or the reformat. `_case_statuses` itself handles the reformat fine — the false red just moved from the scanner into the fixture builder, defeating the commit's stated purpose. The same applies to the `esac` line: indent it and `lines.index("esac", start)` fails identically.

defects.summary: `_shell_scan`'s docstring states a specific "Measured" result that does not reproduce, and asserts a safety property (fails loud) that is the opposite of the measured behaviour (fails quiet). This is the #120 defect class reintroduced inside the commit that fixes #120.
defects.evidence: Lines 214-227 claim: "Measured, by splicing one line into that heredoc: ... a line that leaves a quote OPEN - `x = \"unterminated` - swallows the rest of the body, and the helper then cannot find the `case` opener at all. THAT IS THE DIRECTION TO FAIL IN. It RAISES ... rather than returning a plausible slice of the wrong region." I ran the docstring's own probe at all 26 insertion points inside the Python heredoc (body lines 55-80), for both `x = "unterminated` and `y = 'unterminated`: the case opener is found as code at every point, `_case_block` never raises, and `test_the_case_block_names_every_status_the_module_knows()` passes green every time — 0 raises out of 52. Sweeping the whole step body (618 splices) gives 419 green, 196 raises, and 3 points (lines 240-242) that return a plausible slice of the wrong region and report a false vocabulary-drift diagnosis — the outcome the paragraph says cannot happen. Note the implementation report's deviation #5 claims the paragraph was rewritten to the measured result ("three of four RAISE"); the shipped text still says the unmeasured thing.

defects.summary: "ELEVEN OF THEM WERE RED" is an unasserted count in a comment — the precise shape #120 exists to remove — in the change that removes one from the workflow. It is accurate today but nothing holds it.
defects.evidence: Line 403 (`# ELEVEN OF THEM WERE RED before the scanners started reading code instead of text`) and the same number in prose in `test_a_reformat_bash_cannot_see_does_not_red_this_test`'s docstring. I reimplemented the base-commit scanner and measured exactly 11 of the 23 `_ARMS_OK` fixtures red on it, so the number is currently right. But `test_the_regression_set_did_not_shrink` (line 1616) asserts only `len(_ARMS_OK) == 23`; nothing asserts the 11. Add a 24th fixture that the old scanner would also have reded on — which the same comment explicitly invites ("add shapes freely and update this number") — and the 11 goes stale silently. The workflow comment's own closing argument ("nothing in this repo asserts it, so it read as checked while going stale on the next edit") applies verbatim. Separately, "all 23 cases above" is duplicated in prose in `test_the_shapes_that_must_still_red_still_red`'s docstring, so bumping the assert leaves a second stale copy.

defects.summary: The rewritten tolerance comment contradicts itself within one block: it names the `status=` write as deliberately unguarded, then closes with a rule that would require guarding it.
defects.evidence: Line 156: "ONE COMMAND THAT CAN PLAUSIBLY FAIL IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNGUARDED: the final `status=` write to $GITHUB_OUTPUT ... Aborting is the honest answer there." Line 192, 36 lines later in the same comment: "The SHAPE is the durable claim: an `echo` may be left unguarded anywhere in this step, and every command that can plausibly fail belongs in an `if` condition or a `||` list." `echo "status=$verdict" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` is a command the comment itself says can plausibly fail (it is the one made failable by redirection) and is in neither shape. An editor applying the closing rule would wrap it in a `||`, undoing the design decision argued 36 lines above. The rest of the paragraph checks out — I reproduced both one-liners exactly (`false || echo hi >&-; echo reached` and `echo hi >&-; echo reached`: stdout empty, rc 1 for both on bash 5.2.21), and confirmed errexit also reaches an `echo` inside a `{ }` group on the RHS of a `||`, the one shape the enumeration does not name.

defects.summary: `_shell_scan` only recognises `#` as a comment when preceded by space/tab/newline, but bash also opens a comment after an unquoted metacharacter. `: ;;# comment` is valid, bash-identical shell that produces the exact false red this commit exists to eliminate — and the "WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MODEL" list does not name it.
defects.evidence: The guard is `if ch == "#" and (i == 0 or body[i - 1] in " \t\n")`. Splicing `: ;;# the esac below is unaffected` and `: ;;# was ;; before the experiment` into the real body: `bash -n` rc=0 for both, and the test reds with "an arm of the audit step's `case` has no pattern this test can read, so its statuses were counted as absent" — a message that sends the reader to diff two files over a missing space. The set already contains `trailing-comment-containing-a-terminator` using `: ;;  # ...` (with a space), which passes, so the space is load-bearing and silently undocumented. Same gap applies to `#` after `(`, `|`, `&`. Not covered by any fixture. (I also probed nested quotes inside `$( )` in an arm body, which the model likewise does not track — both shapes I tried stayed green, so that one is not a live defect.)

defects.summary: `_shell_scan`'s comment rule (`#` must follow space/tab/newline) is narrower than bash's (`#` begins a comment wherever it begins a word — after `;`, `&`, `|`, `(` too). The gap reproduces the exact false red this change exists to remove, with the exact misleading message, and it also relocates `_tail()`.
defects.evidence:
scripts/test_account_workflows.py:253 `if ch == "#" and (i == 0 or body[i - 1] in " 	
")`. Bash's real rule verified: `bash -c 'v=fresh; case "$v" in fresh) echo QUIET ;;# a note with ;; and esac in it
 *) echo LOUD ;; esac'` prints QUIET, rc=0 — `;;#` is a genuine comment. Symptom 1 (false red, wrong accusation): writing `: ;;# quiet on purpose` in the real quiet arm (bash -n rc=0) reds `test_the_case_block_names_every_status_the_module_knows` with `AssertionError: no catch-all arm: a status this repo has never heard of matches nothing, says nothing, and the run goes green having used the local recording alone` — false about production — and `assert '*' in {'# quiet on purpose
  *', 'fresh', ...}`. The _ARMS_OK fixture that looks like it covers this, `trailing-comment-containing-a-terminator` (scripts/test_account_workflows.py:458), writes `: ;;  # ...` with spaces, so the gap sits just outside the regression set. Symptom 2 (boundary relocation): splicing `: ;# the heredoc ends with ) || verdict="" and then dispatches` above the real `verdict=$(` line (bash -n rc=0) makes `_code_index` return the decoy — the hardened slice starts `" and then dispatches
verdict=$(python3 - <<'PY'..."` instead of the real tail. `(#...` and `true ;#...` relocate it identically. That is precisely what `test_the_tail_slice_is_not_relocated_by_a_comment` claims to close; its own decoy uses the own-line shape, which the scanner does handle. defects.summary: The comment justifying the count's removal asserts a history the repo's own git log contradicts: the count never moved, and the third arm it blames already existed when the count was written. An unverifiable history claim, in the commit whose subject is comments carrying claims that read as checked.
defects.evidence: .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml:187 "It was unstable as well - it moved inside the branch that wrote it, when the empty-capture guard grew a third arm". Checked over every commit touching the file reachable from the branch point b81f6f1: the text `<N> other \`echo\` commands` appears in exactly one commit ever — 50eeef2 (2026-08-22), always as "Twelve". It has no other value in history. And `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8edd0db 50eeef2` succeeds: 8edd0db ("Let a pip failure and an import failure be two faults") added the third arm BEFORE the count was written — `git show 50eeef2:...| grep -c 'elif \[ "$pip_ok" = no \]'` returns 1. The count is also still correct today by its own definition: 2 clone-success echoes (lines 25, 31 of the run body) + 9 `::warning::` echoes (46, 48, 50, 54, 177, 179, 242, 301, 306) + the `published account audit reads:` line (182) = 12. The removal's other argument (nothing in the repo asserts it) is sound and sufficient; this second one is the defect class #120 exists to remove. Separately verified as accurate in the same block: the two `bash -e -c` one-liners both print `bash: line 1: echo: write error: Bad file descriptor` and both exit 1; the four echo contexts named (if/elif/else/case body, top level, RHS of `||`) all exist; and the "ELEVEN OF THEM WERE RED" claim in scripts/test_account_workflows.py reproduces exactly — 11 of the 23 _ARMS_OK fixtures fail the pre-change text scanner.

defects.summary: `_CASE_VERDICT` and `_CASE_SKILL` hard-require the quoted form `case "$X"`, but POSIX `case` does not field-split or glob its word, so dropping the quotes is a reformat bash cannot see — and it reds.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:174 `_CASE_VERDICT = re.compile(r'(?<![\w.-])case\s+"\$verdict"\s+in(?![\w.-])')` and :176 `_CASE_SKILL`. Equivalence verified: `v="a b"; case $v in "a b") ...` matches (no field splitting); `v="*"; case $v in "*") ...` matches (no pathname expansion); `v=""; case $v in "") ...` matches. Measured: `case $verdict in` in account-skill-zips.yml (bash -n rc=0) -> 29 failed, 136 passed; `case $SKILL in` in record-account-upload.yml (bash -n rc=0) -> 11 failed, 154 passed. The failure messages are honest ("no longer a command this test can find"), which is why this is a nit rather than a repeat of finding 2, but the shape is absent from `_ARMS_OK` and nothing states that the quoted form is being pinned on purpose. The record-workflow guard scanner is otherwise robust — opener on its own line, a comment inside the guard, and a trailing comment on the opener all stay green.

defects.summary: `test_the_regression_set_did_not_shrink` asserts equality, so it also reds when the set GROWS — contradicting both its name and its own instruction to "add shapes freely".
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1616 `assert len(_ARMS_OK) == 23`. The docstring says the number is "the opposite shape" of #120's stale count because it is asserted, and the message says "add shapes freely and update this number, but do not take one out". An `assert len(_ARMS_OK) >= 23` expresses exactly the stated intent and stops the number needing a bump on every addition; the equality form reintroduces a hand-maintained count that every contributor must edit, which is the friction that makes people delete shapes instead of adding them.

defects.summary: `_shell_scan`'s "Measured" claim about an unterminated quote inside the Python heredoc does not reproduce at any splice position, and the paragraph it supports tells the reader a silent failure mode is loud.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:203-207 (added by 5e323d5): "Measured, by splicing one line into that heredoc: ... a line that leaves a quote OPEN - `x = "unterminated` - swallows the rest of the body, and the helper then cannot find the `case` opener at all." I spliced each of four probes (`x = "unterminated`, `x = 'unterminated`, `"""doc`, `# skills-evals' own`) at every one of the 26 line positions inside the audit step's heredoc (body lines 55-80, heredoc opens at 54 with `verdict=$(python3 - <<'PY'` and closes at 80). The very next paragraph, "THAT IS THE DIRECTION TO FAIL IN. It RAISES, with the sentence its caller passed", rests on this measurement, so a reader is assured of a loud failure on a shape that in fact passes silently. The implementation report's deviation #5 claims this was re-measured and that "three of four RAISE" — that measurement does not reproduce.

defects.summary: The replacement tolerance paragraph — whose subject is why unasserted counts are bad — justifies itself with an instability anecdote the repo's own history contradicts.
defects.evidence: .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml:186-188 (added by 8750045): "It was unstable as well - it moved inside the branch that wrote it, when the empty-capture guard grew a third arm". Checked against git: scanning every revision of this file, the count text existed in exactly one commit ever — 50eeef2, reading "Twelve other `echo` commands" — and was deleted by 8750045. It never moved. Nor did the true count move for the stated reason: the third arm landed in 8edd0db ("Let a pip failure and an import failure be two faults"), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8edd0db 50eeef2` confirms it is an ANCESTOR of the commit that wrote the count. `grep -c 'echo "::warning::'` gives 9 both at 50eeef2 and at HEAD, so the named set of twelve was still accurate when it was deleted. The paragraph's other historical claim does check out (the old set of 12 omitted the `mkdir` fallback and the `no verdict...` line; there are 15 code `echo`s, 14 non-redirecting), which makes the fabricated half harder to spot.

defects.summary: "Every one of those fails loud" is false for two of the three shapes it names; extglob returns a wrong token set and reds with the cross-repo-drift misdiagnosis this whole change exists to eliminate.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:216-219 defines the failure mode two sentences earlier — "It RAISES, with the sentence its caller passed, rather than returning a plausible slice of the wrong region" — then claims "Extglob patterns, an `esac` reached through a variable, and a `case` whose word is built by expansion are all outside the model too, and all fail the same loud way." Measured with extglob arms spliced into the real body: NO raise. `_case_statuses` returns literals `{'@(stale', 'missing', 'unreadable', ...}` (and `{'!(zzz', ...}` for the negation form), and the test reds with "the `case` and account_zip_selection.py disagree about which statuses exist" — verbatim the false accusation that L399-402 calls "the expensive direction... it accuses an author of moving skills-evals' vocabulary". L1408-1410 repeats the claim for `_case_statuses` ("It does not know heredocs, extglob, or an `esac` reached through a variable. Every one of those fails loud - see `_shell_scan`"), which is additionally falsified for heredocs by the second finding above, where the shape passes silently. Mitigating: `@(...)` needs `shopt -s extglob` to be valid bash at all (`bash -n` exit 2 without it), so the shape cannot ship accidentally.

defects.summary: `_splice`'s rationale names a ci.yml mechanism that does not exist and that another test in this repo forbids.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:352-354: "a fixtures directory under `scripts/` would need its own salient-path entry in ci.yml." Parsed ci.yml: its triggers are `pull_request` (no filters), `push: [branches]`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch` — there are no `paths:`/`paths-ignore:` entries anywhere to add one to, and scripts/test_ci_workflow.py:74-78 affirmatively forbids `{paths, paths-ignore, branches, branches-ignore}` on `on: pull_request`. Under the other reading — the pytest target list — the claim also fails: ci.yml:308 and :369 pass `scripts/` wholesale, so a fixtures directory beneath it is already covered and would need no entry either. The in-memory design may well be right; the reason given for it is not checkable, and checks out false.

defects.evidence: scripts/account_zip_selection.py:67-69: "`--audit-status` is a public entry point with other callers, and dropping the strip here would buy agreement with a NEW false negative: `fresh\r` would silently degrade to `unavailable` everywhere". The paragraph's test citation is honest, though: I dropped the `.strip()` and `test_the_step_and_the_module_agree_on_what_a_verdict_is` reds along with `test_any_unrecognised_status_reads_as_unavailable`.
